subject.title: feat: per-job elevated exec scoping for cron and heartbeat

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class per-job and heartbeat elevated-provenance contract, and what creator/approver and migration semantics should it enforce?
rationale: This changes a host-exec security boundary plus persisted cron/heartbeat trust state, so automation should not choose the permanent privilege model without maintainer security/product intent.

options.title: Approve core provenance design
options.body: Add gateway-injected creator/approver provenance for cron jobs and heartbeat trust state, with tests and doctor/upgrade behavior before allowing scheduled elevated exec.

options.title: Fold into scheduling RFC
options.body: Make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/71712 the canonical design vehicle and keep this issue as a focused security requirement under that broader provenance API.

options.title: Reject scheduled elevated exec
options.body: Keep scheduled cron/heartbeat elevated exec unsupported and document OS-level cron or explicit operator-run workflows as the supported alternative.

recommendation.title: Approve core provenance design
recommendation.body: Add gateway-injected creator/approver provenance for cron jobs and heartbeat trust state, with tests and doctor/upgrade behavior before allowing scheduled elevated exec.

likelyOwner.reason: The closest merged implementation is the agent cron caller-scope work in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96883, so this owner has the most direct recent context for the next security-boundary decision.
